correctness.rationale: Exact symbolic expansion verifies the error-coordinate ODE and Lyapunov polynomial identity. Positive forcing in the height equation controls negative \(z_0\) by an exponential lower bound. Gronwall gives global E decay, completeness follows from finite-time boundedness of \(x,u,w\), and x integrates to a limit with explicit tail. Measure and compact-set statements follow respectively by dominated convergence and backward preimage comparison. The transverse matrix has explicitly computed trace and determinant; \(\gamma<0\) yields positive trace for some s. The checker verifies critical algebra but is not substituted for the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The primary article [DOI 10.1038/s41598-023-33826-4] restricts its nonlinear global Lyapunov theorem (Proposition 4.4(2)) to \(b_3=0\), while its more general Proposition 4.4(1) provides local spectral information only. The present original core is a full unbounded half-ray \(b_3>0\) with explicit all-real-data exponential control, selected-limit retraction and complete stationary/compact recurrent classification, not implied by the source’s local result. Related accessible published claims were compared for implication and did not cover this cubic system. The negative-sign trace observation is subsumed by the prior local formula and is not claimed separately as novel.
residual_risks: Complete primary-paper PDF was not available for page-by-page inspection, although the key theorem, parameter restrictions, equations and proof were read in indexed form; uninspected appendices could contain extra material.
Other unindexed publications or mathematically equivalent polynomial normal forms may already imply the same positive-coupling extension.
This is not an independent publication-priority or mathematical audit.

value.rationale: The motivating original 2023 article explicitly sought global stabilization of its parabolic equilibrium manifold, and its only provided Lyapunov proof sets the physically substantive xz coupling \(b_3\) to zero. Retaining all positive \(b_3\) on the natural equilibrium surface, with no restriction on the initial height, gives a useful parameter half-space of rigorous global nonchaotic dynamics, an explicit transient cost, a continuous phase-selection retraction, and an exact obstruction to universal normal stability on the negative side. These are motivated dynamical distinctions rather than a routine numerical slice.
